analysis.title: Following AI's $1.6 trillion Money Trail: Mapping the Revenue Generated by the Capex Boom
key_insights: MS adds lease-financed capex to hyperscaler and neocloud cash capex estimates. Lease capex adds $195bn in 2027 and $246bn in 2028. Total AI capex is $980bn in 2026 (+~100% y/y), $1.58tr in 2027 (+~60% y/y) and $1.81tr in 2028 (+14% y/y). Cash capex alone is about $1.4tr in 2027, so leases raise total 2027 investment by ~14%.

Data center leases do not appear as capex on the cash flow statement or in management guidance. Hyperscalers disclose more than $1.1tr of leases signed but not yet commenced. MS calls leases 'synthetic capex' and says capex forecasts are increasingly not telling the whole story.

MS maps $1.6tr of 2027 capex to $1.7tr of supplier revenues across ~50 companies. It attributes the gap to private neocloud and bitcoin-miner splits, timing differences and supplier price increases not yet in capex estimates.

About 65% of AI capex is absorbed by S&P 500 companies, roughly $1.0tr in 2027. That is ~5% of 2027 SPX sales and ~24-25% of SPX sales growth. SPX 2027 sales growth is 8.6% with AI capex and 6.6% without it, a 200bp lift.
NVDA captures about two-thirds of the AI capex flowing into the S&P 500, nearly $690bn of the $1.0tr. Ex-NVDA flow-through is $339bn, or 1.6% of SPX 2027 sales.

AI names (42 'Core to Thesis' Enablers/Adopters) are growing 2027 sales at 28% versus 5% for non-AI, and 2027 earnings at 25% versus 4%. They drive 60% of 2027 SPX sales growth and 78% of 2027 earnings growth, and make up 37% of 2027 consensus net income. Mag 7 are ~70% of the AI cohort's sales and ~75% of its earnings.

MS says earnings growth appears near its peak, with 2Q26 the peak quarter for both AI and non-AI cohorts, and markets trade on rate of change. It expects leadership to shift from pure Enablers toward blended Enabler/Adopters and Adopters in 2027.

Analysts expect capex to add ~70 GW of capacity in 2027/28 (32 GW and 38 GW), reaching ~145 GW of total compute in 2028, about 4x 2025. Custom ASICs rise from 34% of incremental capacity in 2025 to 66% in 2028, with Trainium and TPU at 12 GW versus 13 GW for NVDA in 2028.

MS is bullish on AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT and META and sees 25-50% ROIC on GenAI spend. A model-enabled API on owned infrastructure shows 70%+ incremental EBIT margins and 40%+ ROIC. GPU rental (IaaS) shows ~60-70% incremental EBIT margins and 25-40% ROIC on a 1 GW GB300 data center that costs $39bn.

Hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT) generate ~$1tr OCF in each of 2027 and 2028. In a capex slowdown with good returns, FCF and multiples rise. If returns disappoint, overcapacity, D&A deleverage and multiple de-rating are possible.

Semis: MS sees NVDA as best risk/reward as the market questions 2027 AI capex, at 15x FY28 EPS, with revenue per GW scaling beyond $50bn with Feynman. Semis multiples have compressed since July peaks, so upward capex revisions could have a larger positive impact. A $1T XPU market is expected by 2028. In a slowdown, memory, optics and small-dollar components (power management, analog) are most exposed.

Memory: the cycle enters its late stage in 4Q26 but is not ending, with moderating price increases, rising inventories and supply growth limiting earnings surprises. Memory stocks trade at ~3x NTM P/E. Amazon attributed most of its capex lift from $200bn to ~$220bn to rising memory costs, so headline capex is partly a memory-price variable. Long-term agreements cover at least 90% of hyperscaler DRAM demand, which would make a downturn a volume air pocket at a held price.

Networking captures about $0.25 of each incremental capex dollar, and ~$0.15 comes from hyperscalers at a 60% customer share. Hyperscaler-linked networking revenue goes from $29.9bn in CY24 to $237bn in CY27E, 63% of networking revenue. Each 10-point change in hyperscaler share moves CY27E revenue by ~$38bn.

EDA/IP: Synopsys and Cadence have underperformed YTD on 'AI disrupted' fears that MS thinks are overdone. Synopsys' new royalty IP model ties revenue more closely to custom chip volumes, though not one-for-one to capex.

Tech hardware: DELL is forecast at ~$6.6bn gross profit from T2 CSPs/neoclouds in CY27 on ~$123bn revenue, mostly AI servers. HPE is ~$2.1bn gross profit, SNX/Hyve ~$1.5bn (~24% of total gross profit), and STX plus WDC ~ $30bn of combined hyperscale revenue (about 60% of their revenue).

ODMs: Value-add per rack rises 35-40% on VR200 versus GB300 while rack ASP almost doubles, so margin percentages compress. Consensus has Big Four CSP capex growth slowing from ~90% in 2026 to ~42% in 2027 and ~11% in 2028. ODMs trade below their 20-year average 2027E P/E of 11.5x, with 2028 visibility the key debate.

Power and electrical: Backlogs across data center names cover the bulk of 2027. VRT is ~90% data center exposed, ETN ~33%, FPS ~65%. GEV gas turbines are sold out through 2029 at $3,000/kW versus $1,000/kW earlier, and order deposits run 20-40%. MS favors tier-one power suppliers (GEV, INIO, BE) against a flight-to-quality backdrop and sees EROC as most levered to hyperscaler spend within Machinery, with CMI and CAT also benefiting.

Financing: The cash-flow deficit peaks in 2027. Hyperscalers issued ~$255bn of unsecured bonds YTD (~30% of 2026 capex). Higher-rated hyperscalers can fund plans (interest coverage 30.7x, 11.9x pro forma 2027 under a $400bn issuance exercise), while lower-rated ones (ORCL, SPCX) show 4.0x coverage falling to 1.8x pro forma. Neoclouds are the most sensitive to debt cost. 2027 issuance should skew toward shorter-duration, asset-backed and private financing but stay concentrated in US IG.

Downside risks: Volume and price falling together is underappreciated. The 2022 memory analog saw NAND shipments fall ~5% while prices fell 20-30%. A 32 GW net US power shortfall through 2028 (34% of 97 GW needed) means the $1.6tr estimate assumes every chip ordered gets powered. Memory, networking, optical and ODM builds are the most exposed to a power-driven pause.

Policy: The midterms are a catalyst for AI sentiment. MS expects a conditional buildout rather than a federal pause, with state and local levers (siting, rate design, tax abatements) binding. Sentiment is most constructive under a Republican sweep and weakest under a Democratic sweep. Tax breaks are the consensus target regardless of who wins.
Upside risks: Wall Street has underestimated secular compute cycles by an average of 38%, so capex estimates may still be conservative. Bottlenecks and faster AI adoption are other upside risks.

Cycle enters its late stage in 4Q26 but is not ending. Price increases moderate and supply rises, limiting further earnings surprises. International memory trades at ~3x NTM P/E.

earnings_insights: Estimate basis: earnings growth for AI names is 25% in 2027 versus 4% for SPX ex-AI, per FactSet consensus as cited by MS. SPX net income growth is 12% in 2027 versus 36% in 2026 (consensus estimates, not reported).
MS says 2Q26 was the peak quarter for earnings growth for both AI and non-AI cohorts. Private AI investments show up in non-operating profit, which skews 1Q, 2Q and full-year 2026 EPS growth.
Hon Hai reported 2Q26 cloud and networking at 51% of sales, the first quarter above half. August 2026 sales rose 52% y/y to NT$921.8B (reported).
Quanta 2Q26: servers were over 80% of sales (reported), and AI is 75-80% of that line. Quanta guides AI at 80% of server revenue for 2026 and AI server revenue to double.
NVDA guidance is 70% total revenue growth in FY28 (company guidance). MS estimates NVDA datacenter revenue of $630.9bn in 2027 (+74.5% y/y).
GEV data center orders have grown substantially over the past four quarters, and its data center entitlement has grown to $400-500m/GW from $200-300m/GW (company data).

trade_ideas.description: Own bottleneck and industry leader beneficiaries that keep pricing power as capex growth moderates in 2028
trade_ideas.rationale: These companies should see upward revenue and earnings revisions even if hyperscaler capex revisions moderate.
trade_ideas.risk: Volume and price falling together if capacity catches up with demand.

trade_ideas.rationale: Backlogs extend at higher margins, and MS expects a flight to quality as new entrants add capacity.
trade_ideas.risk: Oversupply from ~150 GW of annual industry capacity and a downturn in hyperscaler and utility capex.

risk_factors: Volume and price falling at the same time, as in the late 2022 memory downturn (NAND shipments fell ~5% while prices fell 20-30%).
A 32 GW US power shortfall through 2028, which could force orders to be pushed out or redirected.
Memory pricing: roughly a swing factor in the $1.6tr figure, and a plateau in capex would hit pricing before volumes.
Financing constraints for lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds, with the 2027 cash-flow deficit the largest in the forecast horizon.
Data center policy and midterm election risk, including state and local restrictions and tax-break repeal.
Execution risk on capacity expansion at power and cooling suppliers, and disintermediation from hyperscaler insourcing.
Oversupply in optical components and diminishing optical content per unit of bandwidth.
Capex that rises on component cost instead of volume makes headline growth rates less comparable across years.
Power OEM industry capacity moving toward ~150 GW annually (versus ~50 GW in 2024) raises oversupply risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex estimates have repeatedly moved higher and Wall Street has underestimated compute cycles by 38% on average. 25-50% ROIC supports continued spending, and bottleneck suppliers keep pricing power as growth moderates.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth slows from ~60% in 2027 to ~14% in 2028, the cash-flow deficit peaks in 2027, and volume and price could fall together as in the 2022 memory downturn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointing utilization and monetization, or a power wall that forces orders to be pushed out, would break the bull case. Slowing memory contract price growth into 4Q26 would show up in headline capex.

tension_points.bull_case: DRAM is a key bottleneck, long-term agreements cover at least 90% of hyperscaler DRAM demand, and the stocks trade at ~3x NTM P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Price increases moderate from 4Q26, inventories rise, and supply grows, including CXMT, limiting earnings surprises. A capex plateau would hit pricing before volumes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Y/y contract price growth rolling over, since memory stocks have tended to turn about four months before the pricing peak.

tension_points.theme: Data center power equipment durability to 2030
tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs cover the bulk of 2027, orders extend to 2032, and pipeline commentary indicates durability through 2030.
tension_points.bear_case: Bottlenecks in power, labor and supply chain, plus industry capacity moving toward ~150 GW a year against ~50 GW in 2024, raise oversupply and margin risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A demand downturn from lower hyperscaler and utility capex, which would soften pricing and utilization and trigger cancellations at newer entrants.

tension_points.bull_case: Value-add per rack rises 35-40% on VR200 versus GB300, and absolute gross profit per rack grows.
tension_points.bear_case: Rack ASP almost doubles, so margin percentages compress, and working capital needs force equity raises at Quanta and Wistron.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consignment models spreading would lower reported revenue, so 2027 revenue estimates may not hold.
